pairs.why_violating: processLine parses an NMEA GGA sentence, mutates running fix-quality statistics, and writes to a log file all in one function call — three unrelated responsibilities fused together, so a caller that only wants the parsed record still pays for stat mutation and file I/O side effects.

readNextMessage both decodes the next RTCM frame and, on a failed recv, tears down and re-establishes the socket connection — message decoding and connection lifecycle management are unrelated concerns bundled into one call path.

updateWithRange performs the Kalman measurement update, prints diagnostics to stdout, and serializes filter state to a checkpoint file on every single call — numerical update, logging, and persistence are three independent concerns forced into one function.

ecefToGeodetic takes semiMajorAxis_ through the constructor but the conversion body uses a local constexpr WGS84 constant instead of the member, so the function never actually reads instance state — it returns the same result regardless of which object it's called on, which is the hallmark of a function that should be static or free rather than a member.

computeChecksum XORs only the characters of the string passed in as an argument; it never reads talkerId_ or any other member, even though it's presented as a member function of the encoder — it produces the same output for any instance given the same argument.

isValidWeekNumber checks the input against literal bounds (zero and the 10-bit GPS week rollover modulus) and never reads referenceGpsWeek_, so the result is identical no matter which validator instance calls it — nothing about the receiver's configured epoch is used.

CorrectionSource declares pure virtual functions for use through a base pointer, and releaseSource deletes objects through that pointer, but the destructor is public and non-virtual, so deleting a derived NtripCorrectionSource through the base pointer never runs the derived destructor.

PositioningFilter is built entirely for derivation (three pure virtuals) and is stored and released through std::unique_ptr<PositioningFilter> in the filter bank, yet its destructor is public and declared without virtual, so releasing the vector destroys each derived filter through the base type incompletely.

EpochDispatcher stores listeners as TimeEpochListener* and deletes them through that base pointer in its own destructor, but TimeEpochListener's destructor is public and non-virtual, so LoggingEpochListener's members — including its open ofstream — are never destroyed when the dispatcher tears down, silently dropping unflushed log data.

pseudorange()/setPseudorange() do nothing but copy a double in and out, and applyClockCorrection has to read the old value out, do the arithmetic itself, and write the new value back in — the accessor pair adds no behavior over exposing the member directly.

phaseCenterOffset()/setPhaseCenterOffset() expose the raw calibration vector so that every caller re-implements the same attitude-rotation subtraction to apply it, instead of the class offering the operation that actually needs the offset.
